rows.jp: 霧が赤面した。

ghs.en: Kiri went red in the face.

rows.jp: 「つぎはなんだよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "What is even next now."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks roughly 'What next?' The English stacks incompatible focus adverbs into an ungrammatical question form.

rows.jp: 「決まっています」

ghs.en: Miki: "That is obvious."

rows.jp: 「わたしは下を脱ぎなさいと言いました」
rows.en: “I told you to take off everything below the waist.”

ghs.en: Miki: "I have said to remove your belows."
ghs.assessment: Miki says she told him to take off his lower clothing. The English lacks the object of 'said to' and invents the plural noun 'belows.'

highlights.text: I have said to remove your belows.

ghs.en: Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 「いいのか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You sure?"

rows.jp: シリアスに告げる。

ghs.en: So I proclaim with seriousness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says only that he tells her seriously. The English adds a connective and inflates speech into proclamation.

rows.jp: 「これを露出するということの意味、知ってのことか？」
rows.en: “Do you understand what it means to expose this?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That means to expose 'this' to the public, do you know that?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks whether she understands what exposing it means. The English adds 'to the public' and converts the embedded object into an ungrammatical assertion followed by a tag.

highlights.text: That means to expose 'this' to the public, do you know that?

rows.jp: 「この期に及んでおどしですか？」

ghs.en: Miki: "Making threats at this late stage, are you?"

rows.jp: 「馬鹿な。君はこいつの恐ろしさをわかっちゃいない」
rows.en: “Fool. You don't understand the terror of this thing.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Fool! You fail to comprehend how scary this thing is!"

rows.jp: 「これはそのクロスボウのように、初心者にも容易く制御できる可愛らしいものじゃないんだぞ？」
rows.en: “This is no sweet little crossbow that even a novice can control.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You think it's like that crossbow, some sweet little thing that even a beginner can easily control?"

rows.jp: 「世界中の膜という膜、処女という処女を無限に貪り食う……まさに魔物」
rows.en: “It is a monster that ravenously devours every hymen and every virgin the world over, without end...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "All throughout the world, endlessly will it greedily devour those membranes we call hymens, those girls we call virgins... it is truly a demon."

rows.jp: 「ひとたび解放すれば、世界から処女の輝きが消えることは確実」
rows.en: “Set it free just once, and the radiance of virginity will vanish from the earth forever.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If it is released but once, the disappearance of the dazzling radiance of virgin girls from the world is a certainty."

rows.jp: 「……世迷い言を」

ghs.en: Miki: "...meaningless whining."
ghs.assessment: 世迷い言 means nonsense or absurd talk. It does not characterize the speech as complaint or whining.

rows.jp: 「ねぇ……わたしも別に見たくない……」
rows.en: “Hey... I don’t especially want to see it either...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Say... I don't really want to see it either..."

rows.jp: 「霧ちんは黙ってて」

ghs.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin will be silent."
ghs.assessment: Miki directly tells Kiri to be quiet. The English changes the imperative into a third-person future prediction and carries over the altered honorific as an unexplained form.

ghs.en: Kiri: "...oh, 'K."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a hesitant assent. The clipped English slang spelling is unsupported.

rows.jp: しょんぼり。

ghs.en: She's downhearted.

rows.jp: 美希は本気だ。

ghs.en: Miki is serious.

rows.jp: 「……すべてを無に帰すつもりか？」
rows.en: “...You would return all creation to nothing?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...do you intend to return everything to nothing?"

rows.jp: 「そうだと言ったら？」

ghs.en: Miki: "What if I say I do?"

rows.jp: 「なっ、君は、君というヤツは……それでも科学者か！」
rows.en: “Y-you... and you still call yourself a scientist?!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But! You... the person you are... you are still a scientist!"
ghs.assessment: それでも科学者か challenges whether she can still call herself a scientist. The English instead affirms that she remains one.

rows.jp: 「科学とは突き詰めるもの。科学とは禁忌の先を進み往くもの」
rows.en: “Science is the pursuit of the ultimate. Science advances beyond every taboo.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Science is thorough investigation to its inevitable conclusion. Science is the progress through and beyond the taboos."

rows.jp: 「話全然みえない……」
rows.en: “I have no idea what either of you is talking about...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I can't see what you're talking about at all..."

rows.jp: 「背後を見ながらの科学に、意味はないんですよ、教授」
rows.en: “A science that looks over its shoulder has no meaning, Professor.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Science performed while looking backwards is meaningless, Professor."

rows.jp: 「くっ、悪魔に魂を売ったか」
rows.en: “Damn you. You sold your soul to the devil.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ngh, did you sell your soul to the devil?"

rows.jp: 「そう、アインシュタインのようにです」

ghs.en: Miki: "Indeed, just like Einstein."

rows.jp: 「やむをえん……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Can't avoid this..."
ghs.assessment: やむをえん means that the situation cannot be helped. The English leaves 'avoid' without an object and does not express reluctant acceptance.

rows.jp: 俺は乳首に触れた。

ghs.en: I touched a nipple.

rows.jp: 「この爆破スイッチを使うことになろうとは」
rows.en: “I never dreamed I would be forced to use the detonator switch.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then I will use this Self-Destruct Button!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he never thought he would have to use the detonation switch. The English omits that surprise and necessity, changes the statement to a future decision, and invents capitalization.

highlights.text: Then I will use this Self-Destruct Button!

rows.jp: 霧はクロスボウをおいて、トイレに入った。
rows.en: Kiri set down the crossbow and went into the restroom.

ghs.en: Kiri put away the crossbow and went into the toilet.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means that Kiri entered the restroom. In US English, going 'into the toilet' ordinarily means entering the fixture itself.

rows.jp: 「爆破スイッチ？」

ghs.en: Miki: "Self-Destruct Button?"

rows.jp: 「そうだ。私はこいつを、この悪魔の逸物を世に解きはなつわけにはいかんのだ」
rows.en: “Indeed. I cannot set this—this devil's member—loose upon the world.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed. For I absolutely cannot let this... this mephistophelic masterpiece loose onto the world!"
Miki: "..."

rows.jp: 「すべての淑女に安らぎあれ。妻よ子よ、すまん……愚かな父を許せ！」
rows.en: “May every lady know peace. My wife, my child, forgive me... Forgive your foolish father!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Be all at peace, ladies. My wife, my son, sorry... forgive your stupid father!"
ghs.assessment: 子 does not specify the child's sex. The English invents a son.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hm?"

rows.jp: 「どうしたことだ、これは？　装置が作動せんとは？」
rows.en: “What is this? Why has the device failed to activate?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What is the meaning of this? Why doesn't the Device work?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese uses the common noun 'device.' Capitalizing it as a proper or branded name is unsupported.

rows.jp: 「……ふふ、あなたの行動など、とうにお見通しだったのですよ、陛下！」
rows.en: “...Heh. Your every move was known to me long ago, Your Majesty!”

ghs.en: Miki: "...heheh, I have seen through all your actions and behaviors long ago, Your Highness!"
ghs.assessment: 陛下 is the address 'Your Majesty.' 'Your Highness' corresponds to a different rank and form of address.

rows.jp: 「配役変わってるし……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "The cast has changed..."

rows.jp: トイレから戻った霧が、のろのろとクロスボウを構え直した。
rows.en: Kiri returned from the restroom and listlessly raised the crossbow again.

ghs.en: Returning from the toilet, Kiri sluggishly readjusted her crossbow posture.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Kiri sluggishly raises or takes aim with the crossbow again. The English makes the crossbow possess a posture that she readjusts.

rows.jp: 「配線を……くそう！　なんてこった！」
rows.en: “The wiring... Damn you! What have you done?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The wiring... dammit! The hell is this!"

rows.jp: 「絶体絶命ですね」

ghs.en: Miki: "It is inescapable doom."
Taichi: "Heh..."

rows.jp: 「忘れたか、乳首は二つあるということを！」
rows.en: “You forget: a man has two nipples!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you forget now, that there are TWO nipples!"
Miki: "?!?"

rows.jp: 「科学に溺れ、人間工学を怠った……美希君、キミの負けだ！」
rows.en: “Drunk on science, you neglected ergonomics... Miki, you lose!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wallowing in your science, ergonomics caught you off-guard... Miki-kun, this is how you are beat!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says Miki became lost in science and neglected ergonomics, so she has lost. The English makes ergonomics catch her off guard and ends with the ungrammatical passive 'how you are beat.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wallowing in your science, ergonomics caught you off-guard... Miki-kun, this is how you are beat!"

rows.jp: 「させるか！」

ghs.en: Miki: "'Cause I'll let ya!"
ghs.assessment: させるか means 'Like hell I'll let you!' The English says the exact opposite—that she will allow it—and adds an unsupported causal fragment.

rows.jp: 美希は霧に飛びつく。

ghs.en: Miki jumped on Kiri.

rows.jp: 「えっ、ちょっと……っ？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Eh!, what are...!?"

rows.jp: 額に小さな危険信号がともる。
rows.en: A tiny warning light came on in my forehead.

ghs.en: On my forehead, a small warning signal goes off.

rows.jp: 咄嗟に霧が、切っ先をずらす。

ghs.en: At once Kiri shifts the point of attack.
ghs.assessment: 切っ先 is the physical tip or point of the weapon. 'Point of attack' is a tactical abstraction.

rows.jp: 矢が出た。

ghs.en: A bolt is fired.
Taichi: "!!!!!!"

rows.jp: さすがに目視できても反応はできない。
rows.en: I could see it, but I could not possibly react in time.

ghs.en: As expectable, even if seeing it is possible, reacting is not.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that naturally he cannot react even though he can see it. 'As expectable' is nonidiomatic, and the gerund subjects are replaced by an abstract conditional construction.

highlights.text: As expectable, even if seeing it is possible, reacting is not.

rows.jp: 頬の横をかすめた。

ghs.en: It grazed the side of my cheek.
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 振り返ると、廊下の壁に突き刺さっている。
rows.en: I looked back. The bolt was buried in the corridor wall.

ghs.en: I look behind and see it stuck on the wall of the corridor.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the projectile is embedded in the wall. 'Stuck on' places it against the surface rather than in it.

rows.jp: 「みみみみ……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "EarMikiEar..."

rows.jp: 「すいません、教授」

ghs.en: Miki: "Apologies, Professor!"

rows.jp: 「教授じゃないっ！　すげー危ない！　すげえ危なかった今！」
rows.en: “I'm not the professor! That was seriously dangerous! I almost died just now!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't 'professor' me! Super dangerous! That now was super dangerous!"

rows.jp: 「……えはは」

ghs.en: Miki: "...ehahah."

rows.jp: 「えははじゃないよ君ぃ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't you 'ehahah' meee!"

rows.jp: うわ、遅れて冷や汗が出てきた。
rows.en: The cold sweat hit me a second late.

ghs.en: Whoa, cold sweat came out behind schedule!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the cold sweat comes belatedly, after the danger has registered. 'Behind schedule' treats the bodily response like a delayed appointment or delivery.

rows.jp: 「し、死ぬかと思った……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I-, I thought I would die..."

rows.jp: 「ごめんなさい……」

ghs.en: Miki: "I'm sorry..."

rows.jp: 「いや、生きてるからいいけど」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, I'm still alive so I guess it's fine."

rows.jp: 「なあ霧ちん？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't it, Kiri-chin?"
Kiri: "Eh, ah, huh..."

rows.jp: 霧は呆然としていた。

ghs.en: Kiri was overcome by surprise.

rows.jp: 「霧ちんからも謝罪の言葉はないのかなー？」
rows.en: “Nothing to say by way of apology, Kiri-kins?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But are there nooo words of apology from Kiri-chin then?"
Kiri: "...eh."

rows.jp: 「命なくしかけたんだけどなー、シャレじゃすまないよなー」
rows.en: “I almost died. This was way beyond a joke.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I nearly lost my life didn't I, that just caaan't end with saying it was a joke can it!"
ghs.assessment: シャレじゃすまない is the idiom 'this is no laughing matter' or 'a joke won't make this right.' The English literalizes 'end with saying' into an ungrammatical tag construction.

highlights.text: that just caaan't end with saying it was a joke can it

rows.jp: 「……それは」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...that is..."

rows.jp: 「それは？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That is...?"

rows.jp: 葛藤が見て取れる。
rows.en: I could see the conflict inside her.

ghs.en: I can understand her conflict.
ghs.assessment: 見て取れる means that the conflict is visibly perceptible. The English instead claims that Taichi intellectually understands it.

rows.jp: 「ごめんなさいだろ？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "An apology, right?"

rows.jp: 涙ぐむ。

ghs.en: She's nearly crying.

rows.jp: そんなにイヤか。
rows.en: Was she really that opposed to apologizing to me?

ghs.en: That's how much she doesn't want to, then.

rows.jp: 「ごめんなさいは？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "The apology?"

ghs.assessment: The speaker label and dialogue are separated by two double quotation marks rather than a colon followed by one opening quotation mark.

rows.jp: 言葉を押し出そうとした瞬間。
rows.en: The instant she tried to force the words out—

ghs.en: The instant she tried to push out the words,

rows.jp: 俺は無性にリセットをかけたくなった。
rows.en: I was seized by an irresistible urge to reset the whole exchange.

ghs.en: I felt an extreme desire for a reset.

rows.jp: 「やっぱいーや。勝手にお詫びの印をもらう」
rows.en: “Actually, forget it. I’ll take my apology without asking.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Knew it, ain't happening. I'm getting a Seal of Apology on my own accord then."
ghs.assessment: やっぱいーや means that Taichi changes his mind and says 'Never mind.' The English instead claims prior knowledge and predicts that something will not happen.

ghs.en: Kiri: "Eh..."

rows.jp: 「てやー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "T'eyaaah!"

rows.jp: アケスケー！

ghs.en: Outspokehhh!

rows.jp: そんな擬態語が聞こえた。
rows.en: Or at least, that was the sound effect I imagined.

ghs.en: That's the onomatopoeia that was audible.
ghs.assessment: The narrator specifically calls アケスケ a 擬態語, a mimetic word for a manner or state rather than a sound. Calling it onomatopoeia removes the deliberate joke that he supposedly hears a non-auditory mimetic expression.

rows.jp: 「あ、あれ？　あれれ？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Wh-, what? Wha-what?"

rows.jp: 「見たか！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you see it now!"

rows.jp: 「これぞスカートめくりの極み、パラシュート・デス・センテンス！」
rows.en: “The ultimate art of skirt-flipping: Parachute Death Sentence!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This is Extreme of Skirt Flipping: the Parachute Death Sentence!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the move the pinnacle or ultimate form of skirt-flipping. 'Extreme of' is not a grammatical English superlative construction.

rows.jp: 「スカートへアクセスする、指先が布をつまむその一瞬、全身の関節２４箇所を同時駆動させることによって、女子下半身における魅惑的閉鎖空間内に極小の乱気流を発生させる」
rows.en: “In the single instant when my fingertips gain access to the skirt and take hold of the cloth, I drive all twenty-four joints in my body at once, generating a microscopic turbulent current within the enchanting enclosed space of the female lower body.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "On access to the skirt, that 1 instant in which the fingertips clench the cloth, I make 24 joints simultaneously operate so that inside the ravishing sealed space of the lower portions of a girl's body outbreaks a turbulence most minute."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the fingertips pinch the fabric and the coordinated movement generates a tiny turbulence. 'Clench' does not take cloth this way, while the English makes the turbulence itself 'outbreak' in an inverted, ungrammatical clause.

rows.jp: 「この作用により、めくりあげたスカートはパラシュート状に維持され、通常のスカートめくりの数倍の滞空時間をもって下着を衆目にさらしあげるのである！」
rows.en: “This current holds the raised skirt in a parachute configuration, exposing the underwear to public view for several times the hang time of an ordinary skirt flip!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Via this act, the flipped skirt is maintained into the state of a parachute, and via an estimated flight duration many times that of an everyday skirt flip, most assuredly exposes the underwear to the public's attention!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the lifted skirt is kept in a parachute shape. The English uses the wrong preposition and an unnecessarily literal state construction.

highlights.text: maintained into the state of a parachute

rows.jp: 「……先輩はヒトじゃないんですね、もう」

ghs.en: Miki: "...Senpai's not a person, really."

rows.jp: 「だが、その長すぎる赤裸々タイムにより羞恥度は飛躍的に高まり、パラシュート効果の持続時間の終焉は、俺の命に対する死刑宣告をも意味するのである！」
rows.en: “But that mercilessly prolonged exposure multiplies the victim’s shame—and when the parachute effect expires, her death sentence upon me is carried out!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "However, via this endlessly long Nuditeh time the degree of bashfulness swells by leaps and bounds, that when the perduration of the Parachute Effect enters its demise, it assuredly also signifies a Sentence of Death with regards to my life!"

rows.jp: 「命と引き替えの大技、それがこのパラシュート・デス・センテンス！」
rows.en: “An ultimate move purchased with my life: Parachute Death Sentence!”

rows.jp: 「……大変なんですね、変態さんも」
rows.en: “...I never knew perverts had it so hard.”

ghs.en: Miki: "...that's a biggie even for you, pervert-san."

rows.jp: 「ど、どうして戻らな……なっなっなっ？」
rows.en: “Wh-why won’t it go back d-down—wh-wh-what is this!?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Wh-, why doesn't it go down... eh, eh, eh?!"

rows.jp: 霧はばたばたとスカートを押さえつけている。
rows.en: Kiri flailed, trying to press down her skirt.

ghs.en: In a flap Kiri flaps her skirt down,
ghs.assessment: Kiri frantically holds or presses the skirt down. The English instead makes her flap it, conflating the idiom ばたばた with the physical motion of fabric.

rows.jp: が、押さえれば反対側が、より高くふわりとめくりあがる。
rows.en: But whenever she covered one side, the opposite side floated even higher.

ghs.en: but the side opposite of her flapping flips fluffily higher.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that whenever she presses one side down, the opposite side floats even higher. The English invents a side opposite to an action called flapping and fails to bind the two sides.

highlights.text: the side opposite of her flapping

rows.jp: さりとて放置してもスカートはクラゲ状に、下着を露出し続ける。
rows.en: And if she left it alone, the skirt hung like a jellyfish, continuing to expose her underwear.

ghs.en: But even if she were to leave it be, the medusiform skirt would continue to expose her underwear.

rows.jp: まるで下方から風が吹き上げているかのように。
rows.en: As though a wind were blowing straight up from below.

ghs.en: Exactly as if from the lower parts a wind were blowing upwards.
ghs.assessment: 下方 means 'from below.' 'The lower parts' can refer to a person's lower body and creates an unintended anatomical reading.

rows.jp: 「反間の計。今まで味方だったものが、これからも味方であるとは限らない」
rows.en: “The Turncoat Stratagem. What stood on your side yesterday may betray you tomorrow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Have counterintelligence measures. There is no certainty that those who have been allies thus far will be allies hereafter."
ghs.assessment: 反間の計 names a stratagem of turning an opponent's ally against them. The English changes this into an imperative to possess plural counterintelligence measures.

rows.jp: 「この教訓をいかせよ、霧ちん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Make good use of this lesson, Kiri-chin!"

rows.jp: 「す、すかぁとがっ……ふわふわ浮いてっ、ちょっと、なにコレ！？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Sk-, the skiiirt... floating all fluffy! Really, what is this?!"

rows.jp: 「スゴワザですねー……」

ghs.en: Miki: "Amazing trick isn't it..."

rows.jp: 「可憐だ。霧ちん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Lovely, innit, Kiri-chin."

rows.jp: 親指を立てた。

ghs.en: I stick my thumb up.

rows.jp: 「あぁあぁあぁぁぁあぁぁぁぁ……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "AaAaAaaaAaaaah..."

rows.jp: 霧ちんはあたふたしていた。
rows.en: Kiri-kins fluttered about in a panic.

ghs.en: Kiri-chin was in a feverish haste.
ghs.assessment: あたふた means that she is flustered and panicking. 'Feverish haste' describes speed or urgency rather than her confusion.

rows.jp: もし公衆の面前でやったら悶死するやもしれぬ。
rows.en: If I did this in public, she might die of shame.

ghs.en: If there was real public presence, she could mayhap even experience death in agony.
ghs.assessment: The English stacks two modal expressions, 'could' and 'mayhap,' in one clause and nominalizes dying as experiencing death.

rows.jp: さすが奥義。

ghs.en: So is expected from Esoterica.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says, 'Just what you'd expect from a secret ultimate technique.' The English is missing a subject and uses 'esoterica,' a plural or mass noun for obscure knowledge, as the name of the move.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんとか全然動じないからなぁ。

ghs.en: Youko-chan for example wouldn't be moved at all wouldn't she.
ghs.assessment: The English attaches an affirmative tag to a negative predicate and omits the punctuation that would separate it.

highlights.text: wouldn't be moved at all wouldn't she

rows.jp: やっぱ慌てふためかれてこそのスカートめくり。
rows.en: A skirt flip only worked if she panicked.

ghs.en: Indeed, a skirt flip needs to send in a flap.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says skirt-flipping is worthwhile precisely because the target panics. The English leaves the person affected unstated and uses the malformed phrase 'send in a flap.'

highlights.text: a skirt flip needs to send in a flap

rows.jp: やがて、ゆっくりとスカートが戻っていく。
rows.en: At last, the skirt slowly settled back into place.

ghs.en: Eventually, slowly, the skirt returns down.
Kiri: "...hah... haaah..."

rows.jp: とても嫌な汗をかいていた。
rows.en: A particularly nasty sweat had broken out over her.

ghs.en: She broke into some really nasty sweat.

rows.jp: 「パラシュート・デス・センテンスを成立させるための時間は、わずか０．０５秒に過ぎない。ではここで、そのプロセスをもう一度見てみることに―――」
rows.en: “Parachute Death Sentence requires only five hundredths of a second. Let us now review the process once more—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "To bring a Parachute Death Sentence into existence, the time taken is a mere 0.05" and no more. Therefore, let us now see the process for ourselves one more t---"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese gives 0.05 seconds. The English replaces the unit with a stray closing quotation mark and adds 'and no more.'

rows.jp: 霧ちんのスカートに手をかけた。

ghs.en: I had laid my hands on Kiri-chin's skirt and,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese gives the immediate action of reaching for or taking hold of the skirt. Past perfect incorrectly moves it earlier, and the appended conjunction leaves the sentence unfinished.

highlights.text: I had laid my hands on Kiri-chin's skirt and,

rows.jp: 「ちぇやーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」

ghs.en: Kiri: "CH'EYAAAAAAAAAAA!!!"

rows.jp: 「久々に足技が出ましたぁぁぁぁ！」
rows.en: “It's been forever since we saw a kick!”

ghs.en: Miki: "First time in so long we've seen her foot techniiiiique!"

rows.jp: 「ぎゃーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "G'hyaaaaaaaaaaa!!!"

rows.jp: 踵落としが、途中で縦横無尽に軌道を変化させる。
rows.en: The descending heel changed course wildly in midair.

ghs.en: The dropped heel instills endlessly changing trajectories left and right as they please.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the descending heel changes its trajectory freely in every direction mid-kick. The English makes it instill multiple trajectories and assigns volition to those trajectories.

highlights.text: The dropped heel instills endlessly changing trajectories left and right as they please.

rows.jp: まさに蹴りの乱気流だった。

ghs.en: It was definitely the turbulence of the kick.
ghs.assessment: 蹴りの乱気流 is a turbulence or flurry of kicks. The singular English phrase describes a property of one kick.

rows.jp: 「おおおおおおお……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oooooooh..."

rows.jp: 「あなたは異常です！！」

ghs.en: Kiri: "You are abnormal!!!"

rows.jp: 異常者扱いされた。

ghs.en: Treated as one abnormal.
ghs.assessment: 異常者 is a freak or abnormal person. The English uses the adjective 'abnormal' as an unheaded count noun.

rows.jp: 「いてて……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "OwChCh..."

rows.jp: 「行こう、美希！」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Let's go, Miki!"

rows.jp: プリプリ怒っている。

ghs.en: She's in a real huff of a mood.

rows.jp: 「……あーあ、行っちゃった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...aaah, ah, she's gone."

rows.jp: 「先輩のチャレンジ精神は尊敬します」

ghs.en: Miki: "Your spirit of self-challenge is admirable, Senpai."
ghs.assessment: チャレンジ精神 is a willingness or drive to take on challenges. 'Self-challenge' is a literalized, nonstandard compound.

rows.jp: 「うむ。人間いつ死ぬかわからないしね」
rows.en: “Indeed. You never know when you might die.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed. Humans don't know the moment of their death."

rows.jp: 「まぁ、君らものびのびと生きなさい」
rows.en: “You girls should live free and full lives too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, you guys should live at ease and carefree too."

rows.jp: 「うーす」

ghs.en: Miki: "'essir."

rows.jp: 「しかし……仲悪いですねぇ、お二人は」
rows.en: “Still... you two really don’t get along.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Still... you get along bad, you two."
ghs.assessment: The standard English construction is 'you don't get along' or 'you get along badly'; the adjective cannot modify the verb.

rows.jp: お互いに苦笑。

ghs.en: Reciprocal bitter smiles.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that they exchange wry smiles. The English is a verbless technical-sounding noun phrase, and 'bitter' overstates 苦笑.

rows.jp: 「俺と霧とはミキミキを巡って恋のスキテキシュだからな」
rows.en: “Kiri and I are lovemies, locked in mortal romance over Miki-Miki.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because me and Kiri are Worthy Rivals of Love over you, Miki-Miki."

rows.jp: 「そうですね。すごく好敵手ですよね」
rows.en: “Yes. You two really are worthy opponents.”

ghs.en: Miki: "That's right, yes. Really worthy rivals for sure."
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: さらっと言われた。
rows.en: She said it as casually as anything.

ghs.en: She said that very casually.

rows.jp: 「美希！」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Miki!"

rows.jp: 「ほーい。じゃせんぱい、またまたいつか」

ghs.en: Miki: "Yeeeesh. Well, Senpai, someday someday see you again!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese gives a cheerful acknowledgment and 'see you again sometime.' The English changes it to an exasperated 'yeesh,' duplicates 'someday,' and uses ungrammatical word order.

highlights.text: Yeeeesh. Well, Senpai, someday someday see you again!

rows.jp: にぎにぎと挨拶を返す。
rows.en: I returned her wave with an open-and-close of my hand.

ghs.en: I return a merry greeting.

rows.jp: 美希は走って、霧に並んだ。
rows.en: Miki ran to catch up with Kiri.

ghs.en: Miki ran over then lined up with Kiri.
